chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no injustice more severe than an injustice whose owner cannot find assistance upon it except for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
ai.seo_question: What makes an injustice more severe than others according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the severity of *mazlimah* (injustice) where the victim lacks human advocates, leaving their case entirely to Divine judgment. This underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on social justice, warning that neglecting the rights of the isolated poor or powerless incurs a heavier divine reckoning. It serves as a practical reminder for leaders and individuals to actively seek out and rectify grievances before they escalate to the ultimate court of Allah.
